name: Karrösten
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny scenic terrace on Mount Tschirgant featuring historic mining adits, a geological theme trail, and traditional fruit orchards.
beschreibung:
Overview

Karrösten sits at an elevation of 918 metres on a magnificent hillside terrace along the south-facing slopes of Mount Tschirgant. Located in the Tyrolean Oberland within the district of Imst, the community has roughly 705 residents. Thanks to its elevated, sheltered position, Karrösten is celebrated as the sun terrace overlooking the Imst basin. While the valley floor of the Inn and the entrance to the Gurgltal lie far below, visitors up here enjoy an unusually mild microclimate. This favourable weather supports a centuries-old tradition of fruit cultivation, with picturesque apple, pear, and plum orchards blossoming each spring. Karrösten charms travellers with tranquil village life, geological discoveries, and sweeping views of the Venet mountain ridge and the Lechtal Alps.

History

Archaeological discoveries of prehistoric urns confirm that the slopes around Karrösten were settled as early as the Bronze Age. The first written mention dates to 1070 under the name 'Oista'. In 1336, the land registry of Stams Abbey documented the settlement as 'Kerrosten'. During the late Middle Ages and early modern period, Karrösten developed into a primary hub of Tyrolean mining. On the slopes of Mount Tschirgant, miners worked shafts to extract lead, zinc blende, calamine, and silver. Under Emperor Maximilian I in the sixteenth century, mining reached its peak with dozens of tunnels. Hard working conditions sparked the famous Karrösten miners' uprising in 1532. The Parish Church of Saints Mary Magdalene and Nicholas features a Gothic tower with an 1830 Biedermeier spire and a bright 1778 Baroque nave with Rococo frescoes by Johann Wörle.

Getting There

Driving to Karrösten is convenient via the Inntal Autobahn A12, taking the Imst-Au/Brennbichl exit. From there, follow the B171 Federal Highway and ascend via the L244 Karröster Landesstraße directly into the village within a few minutes. Rail travellers arrive at the Imst-Pitztal railway station in the valley bottom, which is only 2.5 kilometres away and serviced by ÖBB regional and long-distance trains. From the train station and Imst Terminal Post, VVT regional bus route 318 operates frequent daily services directly to Karrösten village square. Cyclists can pedal up scenic paved branch routes ascending from the Inn Cycle Path.

Tips

One of the main attractions is the Geological Nature Trail of Karrösten. Beginning near the community sports ground, this educational trail climbs over two and a half hours to the Karröster Alm at 1,468 metres. Informative display boards illustrate 30 million years of geological history, rock strata, and tectonic folding. Along the path, historic mining adits known as Knappenlöcher offer glimpses into the mountain's rich underground heritage. At the welcoming Karröster Alm, hikers enjoy traditional Tyrolean cuisine on the sun terrace and can embark on the challenging ridge crossing of Mount Tschirgant. Another rewarding spot is the Karröster Cross viewpoint overlooking the town of Imst. In spring, strolling through blossoming orchards and tasting artisanal brandies at local distilleries is a delight.
